## Why This Deck Exists

This is a demo of building slides with **Quarto + reveal.js**, using
**Observable JS (`{ojs}`)** code chunks instead of Python — since this
project's whole stack (physics, DOE designs, analysis) is vanilla JS.

::: {.incremental}
- Quarto's core rendering (Markdown → reveal.js/Beamer/PPTX) needs no runtime beyond Pandoc
- `{ojs}` chunks execute live in the browser via Observable's bundled runtime — `d3` and `Plot` are available with no npm install
- Charts below load straight from `course/data/phase1-screening-2^(5-2).csv`, the same file [doe/run-study.mjs](../../doe/run-study.mjs) generates
:::

## The Screening Design

Phase 1 is a resolution III 2^(5-2) fractional factorial over the five
catapult factors (`A` pull-back angle, `B` stop angle, `C` bungee position,
`D` arm hole, `E` pin elevation), replicated per run.

```{ojs}
data = d3.csv("../data/phase1-screening-2^(5-2).csv", d3.autoType)
```

```{ojs}
Inputs.table(data, {rows: 6})
```

## Distance vs. Pull-Back Angle

A live scatter — every point below is read out of the actual CSV at render
time, colored by arm hole (`D`) to eyeball a possible interaction.

```{ojs}
Plot.plot({
  width: 800,
  height: 420,
  x: {label: "Pull-back angle A (°)"},
  y: {label: "Distance (m)"},
  color: {legend: true, label: "Arm hole D"},
  marks: [
    Plot.dot(data, {
      x: "A_pullBackAngle",
      y: "Distance_m",
      fill: "D_armHole",
      r: 4
    })
  ]
})
```

## Filter Interactively

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
```{ojs}
viewof armHole = Inputs.select(
  [...new Set(data.map(d => d.D_armHole))].sort((a, b) => a - b),
  {label: "Arm hole (D)"}
)
```

Pick a level of `D` and the plot on the right updates — this is a live
Observable reactive cell, not a pre-rendered image.
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}
```{ojs}
Plot.plot({
  width: 480,
  height: 380,
  x: {label: "Pull-back angle A (°)"},
  y: {label: "Distance (m)", domain: [0, d3.max(data, d => d.Distance_m) * 1.1]},
  marks: [
    Plot.dot(
      data.filter(d => d.D_armHole === armHole),
      {x: "A_pullBackAngle", y: "Distance_m", r: 5}
    )
  ]
})
```
:::
:::

## Takeaways

::: {.incremental}
- No Python, no `uv`, no Jupyter kernel — this whole deck is Pandoc + a browser
- Data stays live: regenerate `course/data/*.csv` via `node doe/run-study.mjs --write` and re-render, no manual chart re-export
- For the full styled course deck, [course/lecture-slides.html](../lecture-slides.html) remains the source of truth — this file is a template for *new*, data-driven decks
:::

::: notes
Presenter note: if you add more phases, duplicate the pattern above —
one `d3.csv(...)` cell per data file, one `Plot.plot(...)` cell per view.
:::
